notes: CardDemo's account update (transaction CAUP, program COACTUPC), a conversation over several tasks whose state travels in the COMMAREA (ACUP-CHANGE-ACTION and the account and customer details last shown, ACUP-OLD-*, and those typed, ACUP-NEW-*): a search reads the card cross-reference through the CXACAIX alternate index, then the account (ACCTDAT) and the customer (CUSTDAT), and shows both; an edit compares the screen with what was shown and, if anything changed, validates every field (status Y/N, four dates, signed amounts through TEST-NUMVAL-C / NUMVAL-C, SSN parts, FICO 300-850, alphabetic names, city and country, the state code and the state/ZIP combination from CSLKPCDY, North American area codes, EFT id, primary holder Y/N) and asks for PF5; PF5 READs both records FOR UPDATE, refuses if either changed since it was shown, REWRITEs the account then the customer (a failed customer REWRITE is undone by SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK); PF12 reads them again; PF3 SYNCPOINTs and XCTLs back. Each scenario's account and customer files are compared after the task. The scenarios that start mid-conversation set that state as the program itself leaves it (the 'N' state's ACUP-NEW-* are what 1100-RECEIVE-MAP stores from the confirmation screen). Data: the customer and card cross-reference files are CardDemo's own; acctdata.txt here is CardDemo's acctdata.txt with ONE synthetic change -- account 00000000024's ACCT-GROUP-ID (bytes 113-122, blank in the corpus) set to A000000000, the value the corpus puts in the adjacent ACCT-ADDR-ZIP -- because with a blank group id no screen can ever compare unchanged (1100 turns a blank field into LOW-VALUES, compared with the record's spaces), so the 'no change detected' path, PF12 and PF5-before-confirmation would be unreachable. No corpus customer passes the program's own validation (every state/ZIP pair fails the table), so the confirmed edit corrects the ZIP to 66044 (Kansas) and raises the credit limit. Every date the program's own checks accept is passed to CSUTLDTC / CEEDAYS with the 8-byte WS-EDIT-DATE-CCYYMMDD and an 8-byte 'YYYYMMDD' picture, while CSUTLDTC's LINKAGE reads 10 bytes of each: the picture CEEDAYS receives is 'YYYYMMDD' plus the two blank bytes after it, which the LE model (tests/equivalence/le/ceedays.c) does not model (exit 98). So every edit scenario here keeps all four dates failing before that call (most clear the day fields; three scenarios cover the date checks themselves), the first message shown is then the open date's, and each other validation shows in its field's colour, '*' and the stored state; a fully valid edit, a date of birth in the future and the 'S' -> 'N' transition cannot be run until CEEDAYS is modelled for that call. Defects of the original the scenarios expose: a confirmed update writes ACCT-UPDATE-RECORD, which has no ACCT-ADDR-ZIP, so the group id lands in the ADDR-ZIP bytes and ACCT-GROUP-ID is blanked; a failed customer READ UPDATE (COULD-NOT-LOCK-CUST-FOR-UPDATE) has no WHEN in 2000-DECIDE-ACTION, so the task reports 'Changes committed to database' though nothing was written (and the account stays locked); when either record changed meanwhile the program returns to 'S' but still shows -- and will compare against -- the stale details, not the file's; an account missing from the master (or its file not open) still reads the customer and enters the edit state with zero amounts, because 9000-READ-ACCT tests an 88-level message the NOTFND branch never sets; the state/ZIP table holds digits 2-3 of ZIPs with a leading zero (VT50-59 for 050-059) while the program tests digits 1-2, so a real New England ZIP such as VT 05401 is refused; customer 10's ZIP+4 (44803-4279) is shown in a 5-byte field, so any edit of such a customer is a change and a confirmed one would truncate the ZIP. Branch coverage (2026-10-02): 83 generated scenarios (field-*) each start from edit-no-changes, break one field (blank, a value of the wrong kind, a zero phone part, an area code outside the general-purpose list) or two (the message-already-set branches), with the four day fields cleared: a fully valid date reaches CEEDAYS through CSUTLDTC with the picture 'YYYYMMDD  ' in a 10-byte field, which the harness's CEEDAYS model does not model (IBM's handling of the trailing blanks is not documented) -- the run would stop, and the harness now refuses such a scenario by name. 137 scenarios cover 89/95 paragraphs and 310/397 branches (from 256); the 34 cursor WHENs for fields after the open date stay unreached behind that gate.
